beat_player.text: gg {player}. {troop_count} of yours fell to a 1.6 to 1 ratio. Your archers never reached the line.
Took {gold} from the baggage train. Your supply lines were thin, {player}. Fix the logistics before the next field.
Ser {player}. Your timing on the flank cost you {troop_count} men. Bring a better ratio next time.
Good fight, {player}. You held the center longer than most. Still short on cavalry for the ratio.
{player} folded at {troop_count} men. Reserve never committed. Predictable for a field this size.

beat_by_player.text: Lost {troop_count} to {player}. Ratio slipped on my left. Recalculating.
{player}, my archers were out of position. That is the only reason. Next field, same ground, I will adjust.
Ser {player}. You caught my second line before it could re-form. Congratulations. I have the numbers and I will use them.
{player} beat me clean at {troop_count}. Good discipline. I counted every step of that flank.
Well played, {player}. You kept your reserve back and waited. I did not. I am noting that.

beat_by_player_repeat.text: {player} again. Third field, {troop_count} men lost to the same flank. I am not asking for luck anymore. Just the ground.
Third loss to you, {player}. I have the timings for every charge. Expect the fourth to be different.
{player} has now beaten my line three times. The pattern is clear to me. I will correct it before the next field.
Your timing is consistent, {player}. I respect that. My second line still breaks under it. Working on that.
Three losses to {player} and I still do not understand the flank. Respect. Real respect, not the polite kind.

player_win_streak.text: {player} is on a streak. Nothing special about it. The meta is the meta and they are simply reading it correctly.
Six straight wins for {player}. Each one came from the same early pressure. Good. Someone has to be measured.
Your streak ends with me, {player}. Not this week, maybe, but the numbers will catch you.
{player} keeps winning. Whatever they are doing with the flank works. I am watching closely.
Streak noted, {player}. Well earned. I will be the one who breaks it, eventually.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men in one field. Overextended cavalry. The numbers were never going to hold.
{troop_count} gone for {player}. Second line committed too early. The tables predicted this.
Lost {troop_count}, {player}? I ran the same troop mix against that ground. It does not hold without a reserve.
Bad field for {player}. {troop_count} men is a rebuild. Post your breakdown when you can, I want to see where it went.
{player}, {troop_count} men gone and you still want to pretend the plan was sound. I have seen the logs.

whisper_challenge.text: {player}. Meet me at {town} in a fortnight's march. Bring the full line. I want a clean ratio, no excuses.
Ser {player}, the ground near {village} favours a flank. I propose a field there. Send your troop count first.
You owe me a rematch, {player}. Set the field at {town}. I will bring the same mix and change one variable.
{player}, a field at {village} would settle the timings. I can be there in four days. Reply with your numbers.
Your flank beat my line once, {player}. I am calling it at {town}. Let us see if the early flank still works.

fought_alongside_player.text: {troop_count} men held the line with {player} against {enemy_faction}. Clean work. The flank timing was correct for once.
Good pairing, {player}. Your cavalry and my archers covered the gap. Against {enemy_faction} that ratio is enough.
Ser {player}. You stayed in line when it mattered. I counted {troop_count} of ours still standing. Good work.
Fought beside {player} against {enemy_faction}. Their timing was sloppy. Our combined ratio carried it.
That was disciplined, {player}. Do the same at {enemy_faction}'s next field and we are unbeatable. Probably.

ambient_brag.text: Holding {fief} with {troop_count} men and {gold} in the treasury. The numbers are not subtle.
Two seasons on the same troop mix and {troop_count} still wins at {fief}. Nobody needs to guess why.
{gold} gold, {troop_count} troops, one fief. Efficient. The rest of you are simply overspending.
Ran the figures on {fief} this morning. Income covers {troop_count} men with room left over. Plan accordingly.
Post your army size. I will post mine, along with the cost per soldier. I already know which of us wins.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {my_faction} now holds {fief}. Garrison set, supply line counted. Next target already chosen.
{fief} taken from {enemy_faction}. Their second line broke on the east road. Predictable.
Captured {fief} for {my_faction}. The siege lasted exactly as long as the numbers said it would.
{my_faction} holds {fief} as of this hour. I expected the defenders to fold at the gate. They did.
{fief} is ours. {enemy_faction} left the walls with a bad ratio and worse timing. Logged and closed.

player_besieging_my_fief.text: {player} has set siege at {fief}. Let them. Their supply train is three days behind and it shows.
{player}, you started a siege on {fief} with a split force. I can see both halves from here.
{player} is at the walls of {fief}. Garrison is counted, the relief column is marching. Watch the east road.
Siege on {fief}, {player}. Your engineers are slower than your flank. Expect relief before your ladders are up.
{fief} will hold against {player}. I did the arithmetic on the garrison. You will spend more than it is worth.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain over {town} again. Fields are soft, cavalry is slow. Anyone planning a charge this week should recalculate.
Lag on the {village} road is bad this morning. Fix your connection or accept the timing penalty.
Someone please explain why {village} grain prices doubled overnight. Nobody buys that without a reason.
The map is shifting around {town}. Garrisons are thinning. Worth watching before you commit to a route.
Reminder: a full line on bad ground is worse than a half line on good ground. I have the tables.
